(Capacity: 20,478) |champion=[[Philadelphia Big 5]] co-champions |tourney= [[2023 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] |tourney_result = First Round }}{{2022–23 Big East men's basketball standings}} The '''2022–23 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented [[Villanova University]] in the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Led by head coach [[Kyle Neptune]] in his first year as a head coach, the Wildcats played their home games at the [[Finneran Pavilion]] on the school's campus in the [[Philadelphia]] suburb of [[Villanova, Pennsylvania]] and [[Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)|Wells Fargo Center]] as members of the [[Big East Conference]]. They finished with a record of 16–15, 10–10 to tie for sixth place in regular conference play. In the [[2023 Big East men's basketball tournament|2023 Big East Tournament]], they defeated [[2022–23 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] in the opening round before losing to [[2022–23 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] in the quarterfinals. The Wildcats received an at-large bid to the [[2023 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], losing in the first round to [[2022–23 Liberty Flames basketball team|Liberty]]. ==Previous season== The [[2021–22 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 30–8, 16–4 in Big East play to finish in second place. They defeated [[2021–22 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]], [[2021–22 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]], and [[2021–22 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] to win the [[2022 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] championship. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the South region. They defeated [[2021–22 Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball team|Delaware]], [[2021–22 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]], [[2021–22 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]], and [[2021–22 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] to advance to the Final Four. There they lost to eventual national champion [[2021–22 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. On April 20, 2022, head coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]] announced he was retiring effective immediately.{{Cite web |title=Villanova coach Jay Wright steps down, joining growing number who are walking away from a changing profession |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/villanova-coach-jay-wright-steps-down-joining-growing-number-who-are-walking-away-from-a-changing-profession/ |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} Former Wright assistant and [[Fordham Rams men's basketball|Fordham]] head coach Kyle Neptune was named the team's new head coach.{{Cite web |date=2022-04-20 |title=Wright retiring after 21 years as Villanova coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33775177/villanova-jay-wright-retire-head-coach-kyle-neptune-take-over |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
